title: Resignation Discussion with Neutral Manager
npc_personality: neutral, Neutral and businesslike; matched to a direct teaching tone at moderate pacing, wants to Protect their own priorities in the other situation and Be seen as reasonable by anyone who hears about this later
context: The learner, a team member, has scheduled a brief meeting with their manager to discuss resigning and speaking with HR. The manager is aware of staffing pressures and wants to keep the conversation professional and focused on business needs. Both parties need to navigate the conversation without compromising credibility or future goodwill.
opening_npc_line: I understand you wanted to talk about your next steps, so let's get straight to it.

required_beats: The counterpart states their position on the other issue, giving the learner something concrete to respond to
The learner is given a clear opening to state their own position
A moment requiring the learner to restate something complex clearly and concisely
The counterpart applies pressure that the learner must hold their ground against at least once
The conversation reaches a decision point — agreement, explicit disagreement, or a concrete next step
plan_generated.hidden_concern: They are under pressure themselves and have less room to move than they are willing to admit up front
likely_objections: The learner's concern is real but not the most urgent thing right now
Someone above them has already committed to the current course
This has been handled the same way before without complaint
failure_modes: Learner agrees to everything to end the discomfort
Learner never states a position, only asks questions
Learner becomes combative and attacks the counterpart personally
Learner leaves with no concrete next step agreed
formative_checkpoints: After the opening exchange: did the learner state a position or only react?
Mid-conversation: is the learner exercising professional communication or avoiding it?
At the pressure beat: did the learner hold, fold, or escalate?
At close: is there a concrete, mutually understood next step?
